title: Activation & Activation Targets
html:
The point of Data 360 is activating unified data — publishing segments and attributes to the systems where they create revenue and service value. This phase covers activation platforms, activation attributes, refresh types, consent-aware activation, and the audit patterns every consultant must build.

Learning Objectives

By the end of this phase, you will be able to:

  • Choose an activation target (Marketing Cloud, Advertising, Salesforce CRM, webhooks) for a requirement.
  • Configure an activation with the right attributes and refresh type.
  • Explain how an activation creates/updates data extensions, ad audiences, or CRM objects.
  • Apply consent filtering and suppression before publishing.
  • Mirror the pattern in ActivationSyncService and Activation_Audit__c.

1. Activation targets

An activation connects a segment to a destination. Each target behaves differently — know the mechanics:

TargetWhat the activation producesRefresh notes
Marketing Cloud EngagementA (sync) data extension in SFMC, columns = segment attributesOn schedule (or real-time for dynamic segments)
Marketing Cloud Account Engagement (Pardot)Prospects/audience updatesScheduled sync
Advertising (Google, Meta, LinkedIn, etc.)Ad-audience sync (hashing IDs)Scheduled sync; consent rules apply
Salesforce CRMUpsert/update into Contact/Account/Lead recordsScheduled or via activation to CRM
Webhooks / external systemJSON POST per member (or batch)Near-real-time possible
Data Cloud-triggered flow / data actionFires Flow or platform-event automationsReal-time (see Phase 10)

The classic exam line: "Marketing wants a segment of repeat buyers in a journey" → publish the segment to a Marketing Cloud data extension via an activation, then reference the data extension in Journey Builder.

2. Activation configuration

Configuring an activation:

  1. Source segment — pick the already-built segment.
  2. Target — choose the platform (per your licence/add-ons).
  3. Activation attributes — choose which profile columns ship (email, Total_Spend, loyalty tier…). Attributes become the columns/fields at the destination.
  4. Refresh type — on schedule, interval, or real-time (streaming).
  5. Filters/consent — apply suppression rules and consent categories (Phase 11).
  6. Run/observe — execute, then inspect the run/counts in the activation's run views.

Marketing Cloud end state

When you activate to MC, the segment members land in a data extension whose columns reflect your activation attributes. Journey Builder's entry source reads that data extension; every refresh updates membership. Choosing the schedule controls freshness; real-time activation requires streaming data and a dynamic segment earlier in the chain.

Advertising activation specifics

Advertising activations hash personal identifiers (IndividualId, email) into pseudonymous IDs for the ad platform; only individuals with appropriate consent are included. Consultants must keep the consent category and the opt-out upload flow in mind (Facebook/Meta opt-out file, Google customer-match privacy).

3. Refresh types (the freshness question)

RefreshWhen membership updatesTypical use
ManualOnly when you run itOne-off campaign lists
Scheduled (daily/hourly)On the scheduleBatch journeys, nightly audiences
Real-timeAs qualification events stream inChurn alerts, cart-abandon, moment-based journeys

Remember the chain: streaming data (Phase 2) → streaming transform/real-time insight (Phase 5) → dynamic segment (Phase 6) → real-time activation (Phase 7). Break the chain anywhere and the "real-time" audience becomes batch.

4. Consent-aware activation

Activation is where privacy obligations actually bite. The baseline mechanics:

  1. Consent categories on the profile (Data 360 tracks opt-in/opt-out per category such as Email, SMS, Advertising).
  2. Suppression at activation — exclude members whose consent is missing/withdrawn for the channel.
  3. Channel-specific rules — a customer may consent to email but not SMS or ads.
  4. Audit — activation runs log counts and target; retained for governance (Phase 11).

The lab models this in ActivationSyncService: before "publishing" it loads each member's Consent_Preference__c and suppresses rows missing the required category, then writes an Activation_Audit__c row with Members_Qualified__c, Members_Sent__c, Members_Suppressed__c and the filter reason. That three-number audit is exactly what a regulatory reviewer asks for.

5. Error handling and retry

Publish failures happen (target down, schema drift in the data extension). Best practices mirrored in the lab:

  • No partial silence — record each run; log failure rows separately.
  • Bounded retry — retry N times with backoff; never loop unbounded (the lab: ActivationSyncService.publishActivation retries a bounded number of times, then marks the audit Failed_Retry).
  • Idempotency — upsert by the member's external key so a retried run updates, not duplicates.

Hands-On Exercises

Exercise 1: Target selection

Match requirements to activation targets: (a) Journey Builder send, (b) Facebook custom audience, (c) update Contact preferred-brand field, (d) JSON event to a loyalty webhook.

Exercise 2: Configure one activation

Document the activation for "VIP win-back": source segment, target, activation attributes (4 columns), refresh type (scheduled daily), consent category (Email), and what the data extension will look like after the first run.

Exercise 3: Suppression logic

Using ActivationSyncServiceTest, write a test giving 3 members consent and 2 missing Email consent; assert the activation sends 3, suppresses 2, and the audit row records both numbers.

Key Terms Glossary

TermDefinition
ActivationPublishing a segment + attributes to an internal or external target.
Activation target/platformDestination system (Marketing Cloud, ads, CRM, webhook).
Activation attributeProfile column selected to ship with each member.
Refresh typeManual / scheduled / real-time update of membership at the target.
Data extensionSFMC storage the MC activation creates/updates for segment members.
SuppressionExcluding members who fail consent or exclusion rules before publish.
Idempotent upsertRetried publishes update by external key instead of duplicating.

Certification Checkpoints

  • I can match a requirement to the right activation target and refresh type.
  • I can configure activation attributes and predict the data extension shape.
  • I can enforce consent-aware suppression before publishing.
  • I can interpret an activation run (qualified / sent / suppressed counts).
  • I can implement bounded retry + audit in ActivationSyncService.

Self-Check

  1. Q: Where do segment members land when activated to Marketing Cloud? — A: A data extension, populated per the activation's attributes and refresh type.
  2. Q: A customer opted out of email but is in the win-back segment. — A: The activation suppresses them via the Email consent category (and the audit shows suppressed).
  3. Q: The journey must react to churn in minutes. — A: Real-time activation, which requires streaming data and a dynamic segment upstream.
